Two-player games on one device

Current NoCharge Pass & Play includes six same-device games, with direct local turns and no online matchmaking, player names, saved results, or match history.

By NoCharge Editorial·Reviewed by NoCharge Editorial·Published August 27, 2026·Updated November 24, 2026·2 min read
Check the current platform.

Use the public pages behind this explanation.

Open the ArcadeReview PrivacyKeyboard-only play notes

Bottom line: NoCharge Pass & Play is local turn-taking for two people sharing one device. The current V2 set has six games, no online matchmaking, and no saved match record or history.

Current two-player titles

  • Checkers
  • Dots & Boxes
  • Gomoku
  • Nine Men’s Morris
  • Pass the Picture
  • Reversi

These are open-information boards or a shared drawing; the current set has no hidden-hand game that needs a pass-device privacy screen. Each page shows a player or artist turn in its own status area. There is no single handoff overlay used across every title.

What “same device” means

Both players use the same browser page and take turns through the controls on that page. The games do not create an account, contact an online opponent, synchronize across devices, or offer an AI player. A reload or a new game resets the active board; names, scores, and match history are not saved by the current V2 implementation.

Choose a game by its rules

For a line-building contest, try Gomoku or Dots & Boxes. For placement and capture rules, choose Checkers, Reversi, or Nine Men’s Morris. Pass the Picture is a shared drawing activity with a turn count and an optional SVG download.

The visible result is the active session, not a durable record. See the Privacy page for the current V2 browser-storage and external-link summary.
